title: Student Survey Questionnaire
purpose: This survey aims to assess the work environment, management efficiency, and resource adequacy within the Law Discipline. Your feedback is essential for the Self-Assessment Report (SAR) required for BAC Accreditation.
confidentiality: This survey is strictly anonymous. Data will be aggregated for quality assurance purposes only. No individual will be identified in the reporting.
scale: 1 = Strongly Disagree / Very Poor | 2 = Disagree / Poor | 3 = Neutral / Average | 4 = Agree / Good | 5 = Strongly Agree / Excellent

questions.text: The academic calendar (class start dates, exam schedules) is strictly followed without unexpected delays.
The class size in theory courses (max 40 students) is appropriate for effective learning.
The class size in practical/tutorial courses (max 20 students) allows for individual attention.
The institution has a clear policy to address sexual harassment, and I feel safe on campus.
I am aware of the program's vision, mission, and objectives.
The curriculum provides contemporary knowledge of substantive and procedural law.
Research Skills: The coursework has improved my ability to conduct legal research.
Communication Skills: The program effectively develops my oral advocacy and written communication skills.
Problem Solving: The curriculum enhances my ability to analyze facts and solve legal problems.
Ethical Development: The program emphasizes legal ethics and moral responsibility.
General Education: The non-law courses (e.g., English, ICT, History) are relevant and useful.
The internship/practical training component is well-structured and beneficial.
Teachers use interactive methods (e.g., case studies, group discussions) rather than just lecturing.
The teaching methods encourage Higher Order Thinking Skills (critical analysis, application of law).
Course outlines (plans) are provided at the start of the semester with clear learning outcomes and assessment rubrics.
I receive timely feedback on my assignments and mid-term exams to help me improve.
The assessment methods (exams, assignments) fairly measure what I have learned.
Moot Court: There are sufficient opportunities and facilities (Moot Court Room) to practice mooting and mock trials.
Co-Curriculars: The department encourages participation in debating, negotiation, and public speaking.
Counseling: Academic guidance and career counseling are available to help plan my legal career.
Library: The library has an adequate collection of law books, journals, and access to legal databases.
IT Facilities: The computer labs and internet facilities are adequate for my legal research needs.
There is a transparent and fair mechanism to handle student grievances (e.g., grades, harassment).
Faculty members are knowledgeable and up-to-date in their legal fields.
Faculty members are accessible for consultation outside of class hours.
Guest speakers (practitioners, judges) are invited to bridge the gap between theory and practice.

29. Do you feel the program is adequately preparing you for the legal profession?
